reading.body:
New Hampshire's tracked data center infrastructure consists of a single facility, operated by Phillips Exeter Academy in Rockingham County, with zero megawatts of recorded capacity.

A total_mw value of zero most likely reflects missing measurement data rather than a genuinely powerless building. A functioning data center requires electricity to operate, so the absence of a figure is a gap in the record, not a physical fact. That distinction matters here because power draw is the variable that connects a facility to grid load and, upstream of that, to AI compute capacity.

What the data establishes is the presence of one known facility under an academic operator. It says nothing about the workloads running inside, the contracted utility capacity, or whether the site supports any AI-related compute at all. A school-operated data center is far more likely to serve institutional IT needs than large-scale model training, but the data does not confirm either. Readers wanting to assess New Hampshire's role in AI infrastructure will need capacity and workload figures this record does not yet contain.
